headline: Inference-time wrappers proliferate — TrustVLA, SEAM and friends steer frozen VLAs without retraining

insights.title: The frozen-VLA wrapper is now a design pattern of its own
insights.body: This scan added three inference-time methods that leave the base policy untouched and intervene at rollout: TrustVLA (mechanism-guided backdoor defense, recovering LIBERO SR to 97.6/90.6/88.6/84.0 under BadVLA attacks), SEAM (training-free smooth execution, jerk -28%), and VIA (Stanford visual-interface agent, LIBERO-Goal 96.7 zero-shot). Together with the earlier CTRL-STEER / PaCo-VLA / Harness-VLA lineage, wrappers now form a distinct tracked category — reliability and safety bolted onto models you don't have to retrain.

insights.title: Efficiency work shifts from quantization to temporal redundancy
insights.body: Two accepted models attack compute by pruning the time axis rather than the weights: TR-VLA reduces temporal redundancy for a π0.5 2-step policy (LIBERO 93.8, RoboTwin v2 81.5), and ChunkFlow enforces continuity-consistent chunk learning (LIBERO-Long 93.4, CALVIN 4.30). Meanwhile Jetson-PI — a pure llama.cpp-style edge runtime — was rejected as a deployment system, keeping the tracker to policy contributions.

insights.title: 339 models, all eight benchmarks live, LIBERO top tier frozen
insights.body: The tracker crossed 339 PDF-verified models this week. Vanilla LIBERO remains saturated — the visible top-13 was unchanged again (cutoff 98.67), reinforcing why LIBERO-Plus (now 24+ models) and RoboTwin v2 are becoming the discriminating axes. The strongest newcomer, TS-Mask VLA (IROS 2026, discrete diffusion), lands at 95.7 — competitive but well outside the compressed leaderboard head.
